profile_text.body:
Thinking Machines Lab is an artificial intelligence research and product company, according to its own site. It is a for-profit startup founded in 2025 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. The company describes its aim as building a future where everyone has access to the knowledge and tools to make AI work for their own needs and goals, and says it is working to make AI systems more widely understood, customizable, and generally capable. It points to gaps it wants to close: scientific understanding of frontier systems lagging behind capabilities, knowledge of how systems are trained concentrated in a few top research labs, and difficulty for people in customizing systems to their own needs and values.

The site says the team is made up of scientists, engineers, and builders who have worked on products including ChatGPT and Character.ai, open-weights models such as Mistral, and open source projects including PyTorch, OpenAI Gym, Fairseq, and Segment Anything. Stated priorities include multimodal systems built for human-AI collaboration rather than fully autonomous systems, more adaptable and personalized AI, frontier models in domains such as science and programming, and an empirical approach to safety that combines proactive research with real-world testing, red-teaming, and post-deployment monitoring. The company says it plans to publish technical blog posts, papers, and code, and to share code, datasets, and model specs to accelerate external alignment research.

The held facts list no lawsuits and no MCP servers for the company. They record a law exposure count of 264 in California, with no individual cases named.
